subject: Request: Time-bound market carveout + deep discount for Pegasus (exec waiver needed)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@pegasusenergy.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Time-bound market carveout + deep discount for Pegasus (exec waiver needed)

Ben, Marissa — looping you both in. Quick summary up front: Pegasus Energy (large oil & gas trading group) is asking for a six-month, West Coast-only go-to-market carveout (no reseller/distributor outreach in CA/OR/WA) plus a tiered all-in per-token discount that bottoms out at ~38% off our list hosted API rates for the first 12 months. They are also requesting a bilateral benchmarking clause that requires Redwood to report unit price data to an agreed benchmark panel and a broad-most-favored-like parity clause that would let them equalize pricing if a competitor offers lower per-token rates in the same region.

Why this is time-sensitive: they want to include the clause in an SOW by Friday to align with their Q2 budget. Deal economics: ARR equivalent on committed usage is $1.6M over year one with a meaningful expansion upside if we accept the carveout.

Attachments: Pegasus_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW + commercial term sheet), pegasus_pricing_breakdown_q1.xlsx (customer-proposed pricing math).

I think we should consider a targeted exception but with guardrails: limit exclusivity to a temporary regional window, cap the discount to volume tranches with rollback triggers, and convert the MFN-style ask into a narrow price-protection tied to a transparent benchmark (not open-ended MFN).

Ask: I need an exec waiver/approved exception to proceed with the proposed commercial counter (see below) so we can close quickly. If execs sign off, I'll propose the counter to Pegasus legal with our limited carveout language and an expiry on exclusivity.

Proposed counter (for quick review):
- Time window: 6 months from go-live; territory: CA/OR/WA only.
- Discount: pilot tranche: 30% off list for first 6 months up to committed volume; subsequent months step down to 20% unless utilization exceeds baseline, then step to 25%.
- Benchmarking: monthly transparent report of per-token net price for Pegasus only; no third-party panel or external benchmarking triggers.
- MFN: remove broad MFN. Instead offer "best-effort parity" for identical product+SLA within the same territory for deals > $1M ARR, with a one-way notice and 30-day cure window.
- Termination: Redwood may terminate carveout early if product availability or capacity constraints materially change.

If you think this is too risky, Marissa, please flag exact redlines and we can escalate formally to Laura for exec sign-off. Jordan (cc'd) — confirming you and your procurement lead are ok to accept a 6-month time-boxed carveout if we include these guardrails?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
A: +1 415 555 0198

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Time-bound market carveout + deep discount for Pegasus (exec waiver needed)

Diego — thanks for the concise ask. Quick risk/impact bullets from Deal Desk: 
- Revenue impact: at proposed 30% pilot discount the near-term ARR math is ok, but if they drive >150% of committed volume the blended realized price drops below our quantized cost assumptions given current GPU mix.
- Margin risk: the MFN-style parity (if left broad) would create trailing price pressure across similar tiers.
- Channel impact: carveout creates potential conflict with two west-coast resellers (WestGrid, NovaRes) who currently have regional outreach; legal and partner teams will want written carveout scope.

Mitigations we recommend before exec waiver: 
1) Add a monthly utilization cap rollback at 150% of committed baseline where discount resets to standard T&Cs.
2) Limit any parity obligation to identical service (same model family, same SLA, same support level).
3) Require Pegasus to sign a no-solicit clause for our channel partners in the carveout territory.

If we get exec sign-off, recommend we attach a strict schedule for ramp and a 30-day review checkpoint to re-evaluate.

Ben
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Time-bound market carveout + deep discount for Pegasus (exec waiver needed)

Diego/Ben — legal has reviewed the customer SOW and commercial term sheet. High-level legal flags: 
1) MFN/Parity language as proposed by the buyer is open-ended and enforceable across future products — this is a high-risk clause for us. We cannot accept broad MFN or any clause that requires us to retroactively disclose competitor agreements.
2) Benchmarking panel request (third-party benchmarking or audit rights) is a confidentiality and IP exposure risk; we should refuse third-party benchmarking and offer a Redwood-generated monthly price report for the contracted SKU only.
3) Exclusivity: time-boxed exclusivity can be acceptable only with two conditions: (a) explicit cap on scope (geography + product SKUs), and (b) automatic expiration with no renewal without exec re-approval. Also include a firm capacity-reserve clause for Redwood and a force-majeure/capacity-exhaustion termination right.
4) No-solicit of partners: we can include a mutual non-solicit for 9 months limited to named partner accounts.

Suggested redlines to present to Pegasus legal: 
- Remove MFN. Replace with a narrowly-scoped market parity commitment limited to identical SKU+SLA, applicable only during the 6-month window, and only if Redwood is offered materially lower commercial pricing in writing for the identical product in the same territory. Provide Redwood a 30-day cure period.
- Decline third-party benchmarking; commit to Redwood-generated monthly pricing confirmation.
- Exclusivity to be territorial and explicit; include termination triggers for capacity or strategic repricing.

From a legal standpoint this is escalate-to-exec territory due to the combination of open MFN + exclusivity + benchmarking. Laura — please confirm whether you are comfortable granting the exec waiver on the proposed counter (Diego's bullets + Ben/Marissa mitigations). If yes, Laura's explicit approval language should be copied into the SOW addendum.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Specific approval requested: 
- Approve the limited counter-proposal: 6-month CA/OR/WA exclusivity window; pilot discount capped at 30% for first 6 months with automatic rollback triggers (monthly cap at 150% committed baseline) and a step-down to 20% thereafter unless utilization justifies 25%.
- Approve the legal redlines: remove broad MFN and replace with the narrow parity language as outlined by Marissa (identical SKU+SLA, 30-day cure, no third-party benchmarking).

Approval format needed: please reply-all with one of the following: APPROVE EXEC WAIVER / APPROVE WITH MODIFICATION (explain) / DECLINE. If APPROVE, please include the exact wording you authorize us to include in the SOW addendum (we will paste it verbatim).
